decisions.summary: _trim_to_service loses its two vertex-popping loops; the existing two-pass 4 ft walk is the one pull-back for every end, popping a vertex only once the end is within 4 ft of it; the comment above the walk is rewritten to say so; the claim line stands unchanged.
decisions.why: This is 385 T126, an open non-process task moved into 405 by the GM's routing ('everything else moves into a new feature') and worked as 385 worked its tasks (FR-001). It brings the code into line with its own unchanged claim and the 0246 research ('pulled back to the last house it serves'), which the impl-drift round recorded DRIFTED. Nothing the request or the spec asks for is narrowed: no end, lane or case is excluded, and the claim is not weakened.

decisions.summary: Exit (e) conform the code to the claim rather than amend the claim; a coarser walk step was weighed and refused, keeping the existing 4 ft grain.
decisions.why: Conforming to the stated claim and research keeps existing documented behavior the request does not touch; refusing a coarser step changes nothing and carves out no case.

decisions.summary: A unit test red at HEAD on a run whose long last segment passes a house within 60 ft partway; claims round on the changed unit; gate and landing cohort.
decisions.why: Verification that only fails when the fixed behavior is absent - enforcement of the task, plus the standing 385 per-task checks FR-001 carries; no new behavior, map or tier is added.

decisions.summary: The plan is written one section per task, each at that task's start, against docs/approach-checklist.md.
decisions.why: A drafting convention for the plan document; it narrows nothing the request or FR-001 (each task worked as 385 worked its tasks, checklist part A answered) asks for.

decisions.summary: Lands open: T01-T31 - the feature may reach main with any of its 31 tasks still open.
decisions.why: The GM's 2026-10-20 start asks for one claim fixed and then the numbers reviewed before deciding what next (FR-004, SC-002: a report before a second task), so landing with the remaining tasks open is what was asked. Declaring a task may land open does not drop it: SC-001 still requires every task ticked, and no task is removed or exempted from FR-001/FR-002.
